newsitem.title: USA: PG&E says nuke rate plan could cut earnings.
newsitem.headline: PG&E says nuke rate plan could cut earnings.

text.p: Pacific Gas and Electric Corp (PG&E) said a proposed decision by the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) on rates for power from its Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant could hurt the company's earnings.
In a filing to the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday, PG&E estimated the CPUC plan would cut its 1997 earnings by 5 cents a share compared with its budget.
It did not disclose its 1997 budget in the filing.
PG&E said the preliminary CPUC ruling differs from its own proposed Diablo Canyon rate settlement because it adopts a "cost of service" method for determining rates.
PG&E would rather use a fixed forecast of prices for the 1997-2001 period.
The CPUC proposes to adjust rates annually to incorporate the plant's actual operating costs and capacity utilization.
In addition, the proposed ruling uses an expense escalation rate of 1.5 percent a year, instead of PG&E's proposed 3.1 percent.
The CPUC plan also excludes sunk cost items totaling $160 million from the utility's revenue requirement, PG&E said.
The CPUC is expected to make a final decision on the Diablo Canyon settlement April 9.
In December, the company confirmed using an earnings per share target of $1.87 as a benchmark for employee compensation programs in 1997.

PG&E also said at the same time its 1997 earnings would be hurt by a higher effective tax rate since low earnings in 1996 would reduce the company's deduction for state taxes against 1997 federal taxes.
In 1996, PG&E reported net income of $1.75 per share, compared with $2.99 in 1995.
